newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco board OKs rail extension project.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco board OKs rail extension project.

text.p: The San Francisco Board of Supervisors on Monday approved an agreement with the Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) District committing up to $200 million in airport funds toward a $1.2 billion rail project.
BART Board President Dan Richard said the vote was the "final local step in securing the necessary federal funding for the airport extension project."

The BART board of directors and the San Francisco Airport Commission approved the agreement last month, less than two weeks after federal aviation officials confirmed the eligibility of airport funding for the project.

"With this final local approval behind us, the next step is to receive a federal commitment in the form of a full-funding grant agreement from the Federal Transit Administration," Richard said. "Once in place, we will be off and running with the BART/Airport extension project."

The full-funding grant agreement from the Federal Transit Administration is expected to total $750 million. Congress would appropriate the funds annually until the federal commitment was fulfilled, BART said.

The $1.167 billion, 8.2-mile rail extension includes plans for BART stations in South San Francisco, San Bruno and at the San Francisco International Airport. The airport line would open in the year 2000, planners said.
